1 · Make one fold table

Split individuals once cv_folds()

cv_folds(data, id, by = NULL, v = 5, repeats = 1, strata = NULL, seed = NULL)

Assigns every individual (not every row) to one of v folds, within each group, independently in each repeat.

idherdA1AA2A……B1B……
→
Repeat1
A3315244251
B32124513
Repeat2
A5142354132
B32341152
  • Each individual appears exactly once per repeat; fold sizes differ by at most one.
  • Repeats are independent: an individual moves between folds.
  • All records of an individual stay in one fold (repeated records).
folds <- cv_folds(phe, id = "id", by = "herd",
  v = 5, repeats = 10, seed = 123)
folds   # herd | id | rep | fold

Left: Fold1 of adg and of bf contain different animals, so a single-trait and a two-trait model are compared on different individuals. Right: every trait, trait pair and model takes its split from the same table, matched by ID.

Pairing by repeat (and fold) is only valid when the validation individuals are identical.

Stratify and extend cv_folds()

strata = "sex"

Spreads a factor evenly over the folds. Must be constant within an individual; numeric columns are binned at quantiles.

Repeats are generated one after another: increasing repeats keeps the existing repeats, so finished runs stay valid.

2 · Build training and validation sets

Five GBLUP scenarios in one call cv_scenarios()

cv_scenarios(data, cols, id, group, folds = NULL, v = 5, repeats = 1, seed = NULL, scenarios = c("st_sp", "st_mp", "mt_sp", "mt_mp", "mt_bt"))

Every scenario returns param (all records, for variance components) and cv (train / validate per group × repeat × fold). All five validate the same individuals — compare the A rows below.

All files keep every non-trait column (including herd) in the original order, and keep rows with missing phenotypes, so the layout is the same across scenarios. Two-trait values are value1, value2 in the order of pairs; mt_bt puts the trait in one column per group.
sc <- cv_scenarios(phe, cols = c("adg", "bf", "fcr"), id = "id", group = "herd", folds = folds)
sc$st_mp$param   # name | data
sc$st_mp$cv      # name | herd | rep | fold | train | validate

Cut any nested table apply_folds()

apply_folds(data, folds, ref = "none", out_type = "dt")

For each target group, repeat and fold: validation = target group in this fold; training = target group in the other folds.

target A, Repeat1, Fold1 · ref = "none"
A
B
target A, Repeat1, Fold1 · ref = "others"
A
B

ref = "others" adds all records of the other groups to every training set; they are never validated.

Input: any nested table — rows are matched to folds by ID, never by position.

w2l_nest()c2p_nest()r2p_nest()your own
+
herdidrepfoldAA1R1F3
→
nameherdrep · foldtrain | validateadgAR1 · F1▦ | ▦adgAR1 · F2▦ | ▦…………
  • Rows: nested rows × groups × repeats × folds.
  • Nested rows that differ only in the group are merged; the group column is put back right after the ID.
  • IDs missing from folds are dropped with a warning.
nested <- c2p_nest(phe, cols = c("adg", "bf"))
cv <- apply_folds(nested, folds, ref = "others")

export_scenarios(sc, path = "gblup", na = ".",
  dirs = c(st_sp = "2.1.st_sp",
           mt_bt = "2.5.mt_bt"))
fwrite(folds, "gblup/cv_folds.txt")   # keep it

Summarise accuracy folds → repeats → models

Folds of one repeat share most training animals: average them first, then report mean ± SD over repeats.

Repeat1.31.27.35.29.33→.31
Repeat2.30.34.28.32.31→.31
…

Compare two scenarios paired by repeat (valid because the validation animals are identical):

by_rep <- res[, .(r = mean(r)),
              by = .(scenario, name, herd, rep)]
by_rep[, .(mean_r = mean(r), sd_r = sd(r)),
       by = .(scenario, name, herd)]
paired <- dcast(by_rep,
  name + herd + rep ~ scenario, value.var = "r")
paired[, t.test(st_mp - st_sp)$p.value,
       by = .(name, herd)]
